D happy path: window, valid hello, challenge, both approve, row, commit, acknowledgement (the worked vector: SAS 865 412)
D happy path with the remote approval first
D: three invalid proofs close the window (3 tries); a fourth hello meets a closed window
D: two invalid proofs then a valid one still pairs (tries do not carry over a valid proof)
D (L6): a window accepts at most one valid proof; a second valid hello is refused
D (L7): a REVOKED pin is refused with a valid proof; the window closes and the user is warned
D (L7): a REVOKED pin with an INVALID proof is refused for the same reason (the status is checked first)
D: a PAIRED pin cannot pair again
D (L4): a SUSPENDED pin cannot be moved to PAIRED by a pairing ceremony
D (L5): a corrupt registry status fails closed
D: an unreadable registry fails closed
D: the window expires after 120 s (Tick at 119999 ms keeps it, at 120000 ms closes it)
D: a hello at the expiry instant is refused as a closed window
D: the user cancels the open window
D: the local user declines
D: the remote user declines
D (L1): the peer's approval alone never writes a row; a lost connection ends the ceremony with no row
D: the decisions time out 120 s after the hello was consumed
D: the acknowledgement times out after 10 s; the row stays PAIRED but unconfirmed
D: an acknowledgement with a different transcript leaves the row unconfirmed and warns
D: the connection is lost while waiting for the acknowledgement
D: a failed row write aborts the ceremony and sends no commit
D: a second unknown connection raises a warning and changes nothing (trust.md 4.6)
D: an acknowledgement before any commit is a protocol error (the ceremony aborts)
S happy path: scan, confirm, dial, hello, challenge, both approve, commit, row, acknowledgement
S: local approval first, then the remote one
S: the first endpoint is unreachable, the second answers
S: the first endpoint presents a different pin (a pin mismatch moves on), the second is right
S: every endpoint fails
S: an expired URI is rejected at the scan and S stays idle
S: a public address in the URI is rejected at the scan
S: the user declines the connection
S: D answers PAIRING_WINDOW_CLOSED to the hello
S: the local user declines
S: the remote user declines
S: no decision within 120 s of the challenge
S: a commit whose transcript differs from the one S computed writes no row
S (L1): a commit before the local approval is a protocol error and writes no row
S: a commit that arrives after only the remote approval (no local approval yet) is a protocol error
S: the row write fails after a matching commit
S: the connection is lost while waiting for the decisions
L1/L2: a ceremony with both approvals writes PAIRED; authorize allows a granted scope only
L1: no row without the LOCAL user's approval
L1: no row without the peer's approval either
L1: no network message creates or raises a row (hint, forged status claim, pairing chatter)
L1/L4: a network claim cannot raise a SUSPENDED row to PAIRED; a hint cannot lower a PAIRED one in mesh-1
L4: Pause then Restore (local only); authorize and the session decision follow the row on every read
L3: a REVOKED row stays REVOKED under network events, cannot be restored or re-paired, and only Forget removes it
SUSPENDED to REVOKED needs no GOAWAY (the sessions were closed when the row left PAIRED)
Forget removes only a REVOKED row
An existing pin cannot be paired again
Per-direction controls are independent: inbound scopes, outbound route, and neither touches the status
A paused peer is not routed to either, and a revoked row accepts no control changes
mesh-1 pairs the own class only (class other is out of scope, LAB_SPEC 7.3)
L5: a status value the code does not know denies everything and closes sessions
L5: status 0, 1, 5 and -1 are all unknown
L5: unreadable scopes deny even for a PAIRED row (duplicate, unknown name, wrong type, trailing text)
Fail closed: an unreadable store denies; authorize re-reads on every call, so a recovered store allows again
Fail closed: a failed durable write changes nothing and the old row still authorises
GOAWAY reasons: PAIRED to SUSPENDED says suspended, PAIRED to REVOKED says revoked, an absent row says revoked
A revoke notice from a peer is only noted: it changes no row in either direction
Two peers are independent rows
granted lists scopes in the fixed order infer, manifest, state whatever the order they were given
